fixes.explanation: Nobody's counting sheep here, friend. Jacob tells his household and all who were with him, “Get rid of the foreign gods that are among you.” He's about to build an altar to God at Bethel (Genesis 35:3), so the first thing off the list is the stuff that doesn't belong. It's like clearing the counter before a big bake.

Get rid of the tents? That would be a short trip, friend. Everybody would be sleeping under the open sky by supper. The thing Jacob tells his household and all who were with him to drop is “…the foreign gods that are among you.”

That's it, friend. The household gives Jacob “…all their foreign gods and all their earrings…” The whole pile goes to him. Then Jacob buries it under the oak near Shechem, and they're ready to head for Bethel.

Sandals stay on the feet, friend. They've got a walk up to Bethel ahead of them. What the household hands to Jacob is “…all their foreign gods and all their earrings…” Earrings is your blank, and the pile ends up buried under the oak near Shechem.

Staffs stay in the hand, friend. There's still a trip to Bethel ahead. The verse says the household gave Jacob “…all their foreign gods and all their earrings…” Then Jacob buried the lot under the oak near Shechem. I bet I'd have grabbed a wrong answer there too.

A storm would've made the evening news, friend, but that's not the word here. The verse says, “…a terror from God fell over the surrounding cities, so that they did not pursue Jacob’s sons.” No clouds, no thunder. It came from God, and it settled over the cities around them.

Beersheba is a fair guess, friend, but it isn't the name in this verse. The text says, “There Jacob built an altar, and he called that place El-bethel…” He's in Luz, which is also called Bethel. The altar goes up there, and El-bethel is the name he gives the place.
